assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made the strong-coupling regime of light-matter interaction controllable on a chip, and it became the common language of superconducting quantum devices: dispersive readout, qubit-qubit coupling via resonator buses, microwave photon control. It is a clear new regime of physics that turned into an enabling platform, and I know the field's details well from my own work on waveguide and circuit QED.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 theory proposal (Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin, Schoelkopf) and the first strong-coupling experiment (Wallraff et al.) at Yale are tightly linked. Schoelkopf led the experimental programme and Girvin the theory collaboration, with Wallraff the first experimental demonstration. Blais carried much of the detailed theory, so choosing three of four is a genuine allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: reproduced in dozens of laboratories over 20 years, with a stable interpretation. The 2025 prize recognized macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, which is the natural predecessor, so this is timely as the next logical recognition of that platform.
uncertainties: Four credited names for a three-person limit; Alexandre Blais's theoretical contribution is arguably as decisive as Girvin's.
I work in this area and have close ties to the community, so I should be cautious about possible bias and conflict of interest.
Whether the committee prefers to wait given the proximity to the 2025 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and the subsequent experimental demonstrations of controlled entanglement and algorithms established that quantum information processing is physically realizable. Foundational, original, and with broad impact on analog and digital quantum simulation.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the clear theoretical originators of the trapped-ion gate proposal; Blatt is the leading experimental realization of ion-based processors. Wineland (already a laureate) and other ion experimentalists such as Monroe complicate the experimental credit; Zoller's cold-atom work also overlaps with other candidates.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with more than two decades of confirmation across multiple groups and platforms, and the interpretation is stable.
uncertainties: The entry is compound (ions and ultracold atoms), and the experimental credit is spread across more groups than the supplied names.
Overlap with the 2012 Wineland and Haroche prize may be seen as reducing novelty.
I am less sure how to weigh Blatt against other ion pioneers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light overcomes the standard quantum limit and is now operating in gravitational-wave detectors, a case where a basic quantum optics phenomenon visibly enabled a measurement. This is the type of clean quantum effect I value, and it connects naturally to my own microwave squeezing and parametric amplification experience.
assessment.attribution: Caves provided the key theory for quantum-limited interferometry and squeezing in detectors; Kimble led early squeezed-state generation work; Mavalvala and Schnabel were central to implementing squeezing in LIGO and GEO600. Early squeezing experiments by others (e.g. at Bell Labs) are not in the supplied credit, so credit is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of experimental confirmation and routine operational use in observatories. Timing is good.
uncertainties: Four credited names for three slots, and early experimentalists are missing from the supplied list.
Gravitational-wave detection has already been recognized in 2017, so the committee may view this as a downstream technique.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new regime: tunable flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in a clean, controllable platform. It spawned a major field of moire quantum materials. I judge it original and highly impactful, though outside my core expertise.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group did the 2018 experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity. Cao and colleagues are the first authors of the experiments, and other groups (e.g. Dean, Young, Yazdani, Efetov) contributed important confirmation, so the allocation is not simple.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced across many laboratories in about 7 years, but the mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated; recognition is somewhat early but the discovery itself is solid.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism is unresolved, though the phenomenon itself is robust.
Credit split between theory (Bistritzer, MacDonald) and experiment (Jarillo-Herrero) and the contribution of junior authors.
I defer to condensed-matter colleagues on the relative importance of this field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Katori's magic-wavelength optical lattice proposal and the experimental clocks that followed brought fractional uncertainties to the 1e-18 level, enabling tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. It is a clean, controllable realization of a basic quantum phenomenon with real precision impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori is the originator of the optical lattice clock concept; Ye's group drove the performance frontier and clock comparisons. Two names fit well, though Hall and Hansch (already laureates) shaped the optical frequency comb part, and other groups (Lemonde, Ludlow) contributed.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed in many national metrology laboratories; the redefinition of the second is under discussion. Timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior clock and frequency-comb recognition may reduce perceived novelty.
Whether Ye should be recognized here or for another candidate, such as the thorium clock, is a strategic issue.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bringing mechanical oscillators into the quantum regime (ground-state cooling, quantum states of motion, strong coupling and entanglement with light and circuits) is a clear new regime, and Cleland's demonstration of a quantum-controlled mechanical resonator coupled to a superconducting qubit is close to my own interests (cf. our work on phonons and artificial atoms). It underpins quantum sensing and transduction.
assessment.attribution: Cleland and Martinis (a laureate) demonstrated the quantum ground state in a mechanical resonator through a qubit; Aspelmeyer and Kippenberg developed cavity optomechanics, cooling and quantum control with light. Other pioneers (Lehnert, Teufel, Painter, Schwab) carried out equally decisive experiments, so credit is crowded.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature as a field with multiple groups reproducing results, though practical impact is still emerging.
uncertainties: Crowded attribution among many equally strong groups.
Whether the discovery is a single clean result or a collection of advances.
My close ties to some of this community.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Loss-DiVincenzo proposal and its realization in gated quantum dots (single-spin readout, coherent control, two-qubit gates, silicon spin qubits) established a scalable semiconductor route to qubits, with compatibility with industrial fabrication. Original theory with a clear experimental follow-through.
assessment.attribution: Loss and DiVincenzo are the clear theory originators; Vandersypen is a leading experimental figure, with Kouwenhoven, Marcus, Petta, Yacoby, Morello and Dzurak also decisive. A fair three-person configuration is possible but excludes several key experimenters.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature for fundamentals, with progress in silicon and germanium, but the platform has not yet shown fault-tolerant scaling, so this may be premature compared with superconducting circuits.
uncertainties: Crowded experimental credit among many groups.
Technological promise exceeds demonstrated scaling, and I would be wary of rewarding anticipated applications.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of conductance quantization in a ballistic point contact in 1988 is a textbook demonstration of Landauer-Buttiker transport and the foundation for quantum point contacts used in every semiconductor and many hybrid quantum devices. It is clean and conceptually simple and sits near my mesoscopic transport background.
assessment.attribution: Two experimental groups published essentially simultaneously (van Wees et al. in Delft/Philips and Wharam et al. in Cambridge). Landauer (deceased) and Buttiker (deceased) provided the theory, which restricts theory credit. Pepper is the senior member of the Cambridge group; the supplied names support a fair three-person set.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with more than 35 years of confirmation, which is somewhat late and may weigh against it.
uncertainties: Possible view that the discovery is a landmark but a well-known textbook effect with recognition long overdue or already absorbed.
Allocation between the near-simultaneous Delft and Cambridge groups, and the roles of junior authors.
